description: Supreme Court judgment records prosecution allegation that Talwar was introduced to Vityash Koser in Dubai through Sunny Kakkar.
Sunny Kakkar is identified as intermediary for the alleged introduction.
Prosecution alleged that Talwar effectively controlled M/s Magent India through the proxy proprietor arrangement.
Sunil Jain is described as Talwar's accountant in the prosecution account.
Prosecution alleged Talwar instructed accountant Sunil Jain to arrange registration of Magent India in Prince Sharma's name.
Magent India was registered in the name of Prince Sharma according to the judgment.
Court records an allegation that Talwar instructed / facilitated transfer of import documents to Amit Sharma.
Amit Sharma is described as a known associate of Raju Dubai.
The November 2020 talc-stone consignment was stated to be dispatched by the Afghanistan-based supplier to Magent India.
Supplier was described as an Afghanistan company.
The December 2020 consignment described in the Talwar judgment was consigned to Magent India; distinguish this from the later September 2021 seizure.
Indian Express reported that the seized heroin was found in two containers declared as talc stones and consigned in the name of Aashi Trading Company.
The major seizure shipment was reported as routed through Bandar Abbas, Iran.
The major shipment was reported as originating from Afghanistan.
The seizure occurred at Mundra Port, Gujarat.
Containers were declared as carrying semi-processed talc stones.
Heroin was reported seized from the containers.
News/court material identifies Sudhakar with Aashi Trading Company.
Court material states the importer proprietorship was in Govindaraju's name.
Indian Express reported that Rajkumar worked in Iran and was allegedly coordinating with foreign suppliers.
NIA arrested Sobhan Aryanfar in December 2021 in the case.
NIA was reported as saying Aryanfar was involved in the conspiracy to transport narcotics concealed in talc-stone consignments.
Court material describes an earlier June 2021 Aashi Trading consignment.
Earlier consignment was described as being delivered to an Alipur warehouse.
Court record describes alleged directions from Mohammed Hussain Dad concerning clearance and logistics.
Gujarat High Court material references Sushanta Sarkar's firm Jesus Christ Impex in connection with movement of an earlier consignment.
Supreme Court judgment states Talwar was named as Accused No. 24 in a later supplementary charge-sheet.
